modern: The perfection of moral character consists in this: in living every day as if it were the last, and in being neither violently excited, nor sluggish, nor playing the hypocrite.
original: The perfection of moral character consists in this, in passing every day as the last, and in being neither violently excited nor torpid nor playing the hypocrite.

explained.summary: Good character comes down to three things: living each day as though it might be your last, keeping an even keel (neither frantic nor lazy), and being genuine instead of putting on a front. Thinking about your last day isn’t meant to be morbid. It’s meant to clear away what doesn’t matter.
explained.today: If today were the last, you probably wouldn’t spend the evening doom-scrolling or nursing a grudge from a meeting, and you’d likely say the thing you keep meaning to say to someone you love.
